;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2020 Streatham stabbing]]
**Three people are injured after a man attacked people with a [[machete]] in [[Streatham High Road]], [[London]], [[United Kingdom]]. The attacker is shot dead by police. The incident is declared as [[terrorism in the United Kingdom|terrorism]]-related. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-51349664 (BBC News)] 
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**More than 200 [[Turkish Armed Forces]] vehicles cross the [[Syria–Turkey border]] into rebel-held [[Idlib Governorate]] in an effort to halt the [[Syrian Army]] advance on the city of [[Saraqib]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/turkish-military-convoy-crosses-into-rebel-held-nw-syria/2020/02/02/17651c30-45d8-11ea-91ab-ce439aa5c7c1_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/turkish-military-attempts-to-block-syrian-armys-path-to-saraqib/ (Al Masdar News)]
*[[Sinai insurgency]]
**[[Islamism|Islamist]] militants bomb a [[Pipeline transport|gas pipeline]] between [[Egypt]] and [[Israel]] in the northern [[Sinai Peninsula]]. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/rJyLd2VfI (Ynet news)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Groundhog Day]]
**[[Punxsutawney Phil]] doesn't cast a shadow and predicts an early spring. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/groundhog-day-2020-punxsutawney-phil-prediction-forecast-winter-spring-weather (Fox News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
***The first [[Novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV)|coronavirus]] death outside China is reported in the [[Philippines]]. The victim was a [[Chinese people|Chinese]] [[tourism in the Philippines|tourist]], also infected with ''[[Streptococcus pneumoniae]]'' and [[influenza B]], who recently arrived in the country. [https://cnnphilippines.com/news/2020/2/2/novel-coronavirus-cases-death-Philippines.html (CNN Philippines)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[New Zealand]] closes its borders to all foreign visitors from [[China]] and bolsters screenings at its airports in response to the pandemic. The travel ban will be in place for at least fourteen days. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/03/coronavirus-outbreak-new-zealand-bans-foreign-travellers-from-china (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**According to Iranian [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Foreign Ministry]], [[Saudi Arabia]] has blocked [[Iran]] from an [[Organization of Islamic Cooperation]] meeting in [[Jeddah]] after Saudi authorities refuse to issue [[travel visa|visas]] to Iranian officials. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-saudi-oic-meeting/saudi-arabia-blocks-iran-from-islamic-groupings-meeting-tehran-idUSKBN1ZW0OP?il=0 (Reuters)] 

;Law and crime
*A female attacker stabs four people in [[Ghent]], [[East Flanders]], [[Belgium]] in different locations. The victims were injured, two of whom in critical conditions. The suspect is shot and wounded by [[Belgian police]].  [https://www.brusselstimes.com/belgium/93371/woman-in-ghent-stabbing-attack-will-be-charged-with-attempted-murder/ (''The Brussels Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Japan]] sends [[JS Takanami|a destroyer]] to the [[Gulf of Oman]] amid heightening tensions in the region. The [[government of Japan|government]] says it is prepared to authorize the use of force to protect Japanese interests if needed. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-iran-japan/japanese-warship-departs-for-gulf-to-patrol-oil-lifeline-idUSKBN1ZW02D (Reuters)]
